package_info.package_versions: various vulnerable versions as listed in CVE-2021-20090 advisory
package_info.why_malicious: The firmware contains a command injection vulnerability in its web interface, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary system commands via crafted HTTP requests. This enables installation of malware such as Mirai, resulting in device compromise and botnet enrollment.

execution_context.trigger: upon receiving specific unauthenticated HTTP request
execution_context.file_location: web interface HTTP request handler (e.g., /cgi-bin/; or /apply.cgi)

malicious_snippets.code_language: C or Python (depending on router firmware implementation)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving a specially crafted unauthenticated HTTP request, the code directly executes the value of the 'cmd' parameter as a system command, allowing remote attackers to download and run arbitrary binaries, resulting in full device compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly executing user-supplied input as a system command is a textbook command injection vulnerability, enabling attackers to run arbitrary code on the device without authentication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal router firmware should strictly validate and authenticate all management commands, never allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary system commands via HTTP requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management interfaces may allow execution of a limited set of predefined commands, but only after proper authentication and input validation. Arbitrary command execution from unauthenticated input is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Direct use of HTTP request parameters (e.g., 'cmd') in system command execution functions (e.g., os.system, system())
Absence of authentication or input sanitization in the HTTP handler
Observed post-exploitation download and execution of Mirai or similar malware binaries
Presence of HTTP requests to router endpoints with suspicious 'cmd' parameters

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted unauthenticated HTTP request exploiting CVE-2021-20090 to the vulnerable router's web interface, injecting a system command via the 'cmd' parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the device

attack_chain.action: The injected command downloads and executes a malicious payload (such as a Mirai variant) from an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Device becomes part of the Mirai botnet, enabling further malicious activity

behavioral_signatures: Execution of system commands where arguments are derived directly from HTTP request parameters (e.g., 'cmd')
Creation of new processes on the router immediately following suspicious HTTP requests
Unusual outbound connections from the router to external IPs associated with Mirai C2 infrastructure
Modification of router startup scripts or scheduled tasks to persist malware
file_indicators: /tmp/mirai* or /var/tmp/mirai* binaries present in the filesystem
New or modified startup scripts (e.g., /etc/rc.local, /etc/init.d/) referencing unknown binaries
Presence of downloaded payloads in writable directories (e.g., /tmp/, /var/tmp/)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Mirai C2 IP addresses (as listed in threat intelligence feeds, often geolocated to China, e.g., Wuhan)
Inbound HTTP requests to router web interface endpoints (e.g., /apply.cgi, /cgi-bin/;) containing 'cmd' or similar parameters with suspicious values
Unusual HTTP user-agents or request patterns targeting router management endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor router and IoT device logs for unauthenticated HTTP requests containing command injection patterns (e.g., 'cmd=' in query parameters), alert on creation of new or unexpected binaries and processes, and flag outbound connections to known Mirai C2 infrastructure. Deploy IPS/IDS signatures for CVE-2021-20090 and related command injection exploits. Regularly scan for unauthorized modifications to startup scripts and the presence of Mirai-related binaries in common writable directories.
